hook.line: Tomás has to ask a notary for something, and the notary is somebody he must address as *usted*. The politest way to ask is to say you would be grateful.
hook.es: Le agradecería que me enviara la factura antes del viernes.
hook.en: I would be grateful if you sent me the invoice before Friday.

rule:
*Le agradecería que* + the *-ra* form of the verb: "I would be grateful if you..."

To get the *-ra* form, take the *ellos* past form and swap the ending: *enviaron* becomes *enviara*; *respondieron* becomes *respondiera*; *firmaron* becomes *firmara*.

*Le* means *usted* (one person). For several people it is *Les*, and the verb follows: *Les agradecería que esperaran*.

The English "if" turns into *que*.

This is formal, and it can be a disguised order from a boss: *Le agradecería que no volviera a llegar tarde* is a warning. With a friend it sounds stiff or sarcastic.
smallPrint: Teachers call the *-ra* form the imperfect subjunctive. After a conditional like *agradecería*, it is the verb that follows *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *enviara* or *enviaba*: Le agradecería que me ___ la factura antes del viernes. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Le agradecería que me enviara la factura antes del viernes.
yourTurn.why: After *agradecería que* the verb takes the *-ra* form, not the "used to" form.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a boss or an official: I would be grateful if you didn't arrive late again.
yourTurn.answer: Le agradecería que no volviera a llegar tarde.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, formal: I would be grateful if you replied to me before Monday.
yourTurn.answer: Le agradecería que me respondiera antes del lunes.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn the order into the polite request: *Firme aquí.*
yourTurn.why: *Le agradecería que* + *-ra* is the polite way to ask.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it to several people (you all): *Le agradecería que esperara un momento.*
yourTurn.answer: Les agradecería que esperaran un momento.
accept: Les agradeceríamos que esperaran un momento.
yourTurn.why: Several people: *Les*, and the verb is plural, *esperaran*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, formal: I would be grateful if you explained the situation to me.
yourTurn.answer: Le agradecería que me explicara la situación.
yourTurn.why: *Me* goes before the *-ra* verb, in front of *explicara*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, formal: I would be grateful if you didn't call after nine.
yourTurn.answer: Le agradecería que no llamara después de las nueve.

pitfalls.wrong: Le agradecería que me envía la factura.
pitfalls.right: Le agradecería que me enviara la factura.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *agradecería que* use the *-ra* form, not the plain present.

pitfalls.wrong: Le agradecería que me enviaría la factura.
pitfalls.right: Le agradecería que me enviara la factura.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "would" twice, but only *agradecería* takes it; after *que* comes the *-ra* form, *enviara*.

pitfalls.wrong: Le agradecería si me enviara la factura.
pitfalls.right: Le agradecería que me enviara la factura.

personal: Think of a formal request you might make to a landlord, a boss or an official. Write it as *Le agradecería que…*
